title: Lesson 4: L'heure
description: A short dialogue for asking the time, forming questions with est-ce que, negatives, and expressions with midi and retard.

notes.1: We know that le and la are, respectively, the masculine and feminine definite articles, the. But if the noun begins with a vowel or an h, we use l'. You see how important it is to learn your genders: l'heure is feminine. L'heure literally means the hour, but we also use the word when asking the time. Avez-vous l'heure ? means Do you have the time?
notes.2: Another very common way of asking a question is to put est-ce que, literally is it that, before the verb. So Avez-vous l'heure ? and Est-ce que vous avez l'heure ? have the same meaning.
notes.3: To form the negative, you need two words: ne, or n' before a vowel or an h, directly before the verb, and pas directly after it: Je n'ai pas l'heure, I don't have the time.
notes.4: French does not have a neutral pronoun such as it. You have to use either il or elle, depending on the gender of the noun. In neutral contexts, such as when you are telling the time, always use il.
notes.5: In the last lesson, we saw that le Midi is the south of France. The word also means noon, or midday.
notes.6: Here, the article le means it or that. Notice that it is placed before the verb, not afterwards, as in English.

lines.french: Pardon, est-ce que vous avez l'heure ?
lines.english: Excuse me, do you have the time?

lines.french: Je n'ai pas de montre mais je pense qu'il est midi dix.
parts: de montre mais je pense qu'il
lines.english: I don't have a watch, but I think that it is ten past noon.
But how do you know that?

lines.french: Parce que j'ai rendez-vous avec ma femme à midi...
parts: Parce que j'ai rendez-vous avec ma femme à midi...
lines.english: Because I'm meeting my wife at noon...

lines.french: ... et elle a toujours dix minutes de retard !
parts: ... et elle a toujours dix minutes de retard !
lines.english: ... and she is always ten minutes late!
